visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A close-up shot begins with a person's hand, wearing a thick beige fleece sleeve, holding a semi-transparent white plastic bag. The bag contains several stacked white meal containers with red branding. The background is a brightly lit, clean indoor hallway with white walls and dark brown doors. (2) The bag is placed on a white marble-patterned surface. The camera zooms in as the person uses their fingers to grip one of the knotted handles, or 'ears,' of the bag. They begin to twist the handle repeatedly and tightly in one direction. The person's hand movements are precise, focusing on turning the plastic until it transforms from a flat ribbon into a stiff, compressed cord-like structure. (3) Once the handle is sufficiently rigid, the person uses their thumb and forefinger to push the tip of the hardened plastic strand through the center of the existing knot. As the stiffened part slides through, the tension of the knot is released. The person then pulls both handles apart with ease, fully opening the bag to reveal the white and pink paper lunch boxes inside, effectively demonstrating a life hack for opening tight knots.
